mutants.why: an EXCLUSIVE lower bound must reject a version equal to the bound; relaxing > to >= makes '(1.0,)' accept 1.0. range_halfOpenLowerUpper asserts !gt.satisfies(v("1.0"))
an EXCLUSIVE upper bound must reject a version equal to the bound; relaxing < to <= makes '(,2.0)' accept 2.0. range_halfOpenLowerUpper asserts !lt.satisfies(v("2.0"))
comparing only the shorter component count treats 1.0 and 1.0.1 as equal (the trailing .1 is never examined). compare_ordersReleaseNumericallyWithZeroPadding asserts v("1.0") < v("1.0.1")

mutants.find: const long long lhs = (i < a.size()) ? a.at(i) : 0;
mutants.replace: const long long lhs = (i < a.size()) ? a.at(i) : 1;
mutants.why: a missing trailing release component is value 0 (SemVer zero-pad); defaulting it to 1 makes 1.0 differ from 1.0.0. compare_ordersReleaseNumericallyWithZeroPadding asserts v("1.0.0") == v("1.0")
inverting the release ordering makes a higher release compare as lower. compare_ordersReleaseNumericallyWithZeroPadding asserts v("2.0") > v("1.9.9")
a plain release outranks any prerelease of the same core (1.0.0 > 1.0.0-beta); inverting makes the prerelease win. compare_prereleaseSortsBelowRelease asserts v("1.0.0-beta") < v("1.0.0")
a numeric prerelease identifier ranks BELOW an alphanumeric one (SemVer); inverting flips that precedence. compare_prereleaseIdentifierRules asserts v("1.0.0-1") < v("1.0.0-alpha")

for equal-radix numeric identifiers, fewer significant digits is the smaller value; inverting the length test makes 10 compare below 2. compare_prereleaseIdentifierRules asserts v("1.0.0-2") < v("1.0.0-10")

a longer prerelease with a shared prefix has HIGHER precedence (alpha < alpha.1); inverting makes the shorter one larger. compare_prereleaseIdentifierRules asserts v("1.0.0-alpha") < v("1.0.0-alpha.1")
prerelease identifiers compare case-insensitively; a case-sensitive compare makes Beta != beta. compare_prereleaseIdentifierRules asserts v("1.0.0-Beta").compare(v("1.0.0-beta")) == 0
NuGet allows up to four release components; >= rejects the legal 4-part release 4.8.0.1 as malformed. parse_acceptsReleaseAndPrerelease asserts parse("4.8.0.1").has_value()
'[' opens an INCLUSIVE lower bound; inverting makes '[1.0,2.0]' exclude its own lower endpoint. range_closedAndExclusiveIntervals asserts closed.satisfies(v("1.0"))
']' closes an INCLUSIVE upper bound; inverting makes '[1.0,2.0]' exclude its own upper endpoint. range_closedAndExclusiveIntervals asserts closed.satisfies(v("2.0"))
a bare version is a minimum-inclusive LOWER bound; storing it as the upper bound turns '1.0' into '(,1.0]' so 2.5 fails. range_bareVersionIsMinimumInclusive asserts r.satisfies(v("2.5"))

a malformed range must satisfy NOTHING (fail closed); with && a malformed range whose bounds are unset falls through and matches every version. range_malformedRejectsAll asserts !r.satisfies(v("1.0"))

prerelease candidates become eligible when EITHER bound is a prerelease; requiring BOTH makes a half-open '[2.0.0-alpha,)' exclude all prereleases. select_excludesPrereleaseUnlessRangeTargetsIt asserts targeted.has_value()

the '- 1' keeps at least one digit so an all-zeros identifier strips to "0" rather than "". stripLeadingZeros is called ONLY from compareNumericIdentifiers on all-digit strings, and the bound only matters for an all-zeros identifier (a non-zero digit stops the loop before size-1 regardless). Both "" and "0" represent value 0: two all-zeros identifiers still compare equal (both "" or both "0"), and an all-zeros identifier still sorts below any non-zero one -- size 0 precedes any size>=1, and at equal size the leading '0' compares below any non-zero digit. The compare result is identical for every input
